# scripts/ci/sigpipe-sites-baseline.txt — THE PIPED-BUILTIN-WRITER (EPIPE) SITE RATCHET
# BASELINE (issue #4061, AC4). GENERATED FILE — do not hand-edit; regenerate with ONE
# command:
#
#   bash scripts/ci/check-sigpipe-sites.sh --regenerate
#
# GRAMMAR (closed — anything else is REFUSED, not skipped):
#   "<relative-path> <count> <sha256>"  one per git-tracked scripts/**/*.sh file with
#                              >=1 match; count >= 1; sha256 = 64 lowercase hex chars;
#                              sorted (LC_ALL=C), no duplicate paths
#   "#..." comment / blank     ignored
# THE THIRD FIELD is an AGGREGATE DIGEST OVER MATCHED-LINE TEXT, and carries NO LINE
# NUMBERS: each matched line is normalised (trimmed, internal whitespace runs collapsed
# to one space, the matcher's "<lineno>:" prefix discarded), the normalised lines are
# SORTED (LC_ALL=C), and sha256 is taken over that concatenation. Sorting is what keeps
# it MOTION-PROOF — moving or reordering a matched line does not change the multiset —
# while a SWAP (one site removed, one added, count unchanged) DOES change it and FAILs.
# A count alone could not see that swap; that false PASS is why the field exists.
# NO LINE NUMBERS, deliberately: #4061 pinned bootstrap-agent-machine.sh:3329 and it had
# drifted to :5392 within two days. Per-file counts are stale-proof against code motion,
# and a line-numbered list is a curated list in disguise (lead ruling on #4061).
# A COUNT IS A COUNT OF SHAPE MATCHES, NOT OF CONFIRMED HAZARDS. The shared matcher
# (scripts/tests/lib/sigpipe-matcher.sh) is deliberately BROAD and REPORTS six declared
# classes of correct code; see its header and the run-time DECLARED SCOPE block.
# THE RATCHET: an increase in a listed file, a CHANGED digest at an unchanged count, or
# ANY match in a file not listed here, FAILs.
# A DECREASE never fails — re-run the command above and commit a tighter baseline. That
# is also the ONE declared residual: the digest changes on any removal, so a net decrease
# that also ADDS a line is tolerated.
